title: All-Inclusive Holidays in Krk, Croatia: Guide 2027
metaDescription: Does Krk have all-inclusive hotels? What it includes, rough €/person prices vs half-board and apartments, and who should skip it. Updated for 2027.
content:
## Does Krk Have All-Inclusive Hotels?

Almost none. Krk is an apartment-and-half-board island. Most hotels sell bed and breakfast or half-board, and Valamar, Aminess and Falkensteiner properties run mainly on that model. Fewer than ten properties on the island are tied to the all-inclusive label, and the label often covers only a limited version.

**Hotel Park Punat** (Falkensteiner) in Punat is the one hotel currently listed with an all-inclusive option. It has a pool, a children's programme and a pebble beach. Guest ratings sit around 3.5 out of 5, and recurring complaints are small rooms and mass-catering food quality. Families praise the kids' entertainment.

**Sunny Baška Hotel by Valamar** in Baška is also promoted as all-inclusive for families. Valamar changes board types by season, so check the rate description on the booking page, not the hotel's name.

Other well-known hotels, such as Hotel Malin in Malinska, Veya Maradiso and Magal Maradiso by Aminess in Njivice, and Dražica in Krk Town, appear mainly with breakfast or half-board. Do not assume they sell all-inclusive.

## Nearest All-Inclusive Places in Croatia

If you want a classic all-inclusive resort, the closest options are across the water in Istria. Girandella Resort (Valamar Collection) in Rabac, Hotel Narcis and Valamar Bellevue in Rabac area listings, Park Plaza Verudela in Pula and Hotel Zorna (Plava Laguna) in Poreč all list all-inclusive options. Maistra Select Funtana All Inclusive Resort in Funtana is a dedicated all-inclusive resort. Rabac is about 1.5 hours by road from the Krk bridge. Poreč and Funtana are around 2 hours away.

## What All-Inclusive Typically Includes in Croatia

- Breakfast, lunch and dinner, usually as buffets
- Snacks in the afternoon, sometimes ice cream
- Local house wine, beer and soft drinks at set hours
- Pool access and sunbeds, often a kids' club and evening animation

Premium drinks, à la carte restaurants, spa, towels at the beach and sometimes tourist tax are normally extra. The tourist tax in Krk is a few euros per adult per night in summer.

## Rough Price per Person per Night

These are planning estimates for adults sharing a double room. Children under 12 are usually discounted heavily or free in a parents' room, depending on the offer.

| Type | Shoulder (May, June, late Sept) | Peak (July–August) |
|---|---|---|
| All-inclusive (Punat, Baška) | €60–100 | €110–180 |
| Half-board hotel | €50–80 | €80–130 |
| Bed and breakfast hotel | €40–65 | €65–110 |
| Private apartment (self-catering) | €15–30 | €25–50 |

The apartment figure assumes a €60–120 nightly rate for two to four people in peak, and €40–80 in shoulder. Groceries add roughly €15–25 per person per day if you cook most meals, and €30–50 if you mix in konobas.

## Who All-Inclusive Suits in Krk

**Families with children under 10.** No restaurant searches, no hungry-child waits, and snacks at hand. The kids' programme at Hotel Park Punat is its main selling point.

**Short stays of 3–5 nights.** Shopping, planning and cleaning cost more time than they save over a long weekend.

**Early and late season guests.** Shoulder rates are much lower, and the pool and the buffet make better use of mild weather.

## Who Is Better Off Self-Catering

**Stays of 7 nights or more.** The gap grows each night. A family of four can save €1,000 or more over a week in July against all-inclusive.

**Couples and food-focused travellers.** Krk's konobas serve Krk šurlice pasta, lamb, scampi and local Žlahtina wine. Buffets cannot match these.

**Anyone planning day trips.** Staying inside an all-inclusive package defeats its value if you eat out at lunch. Visits to Baška's long beach, Krk Town's old centre and Vrbnik's wine cellars all mean paying for meals twice.

My blunt view: on Krk, all-inclusive is a poor deal in July and August. Peak prices approach those of better-known resort destinations, yet reviews of the only dedicated option point to tired rooms and frozen-food cooking. If the budget is tight, half-board or an apartment near a beach gives far better value.

## Practical Tips

- Book all-inclusive for Krk by early spring. Few rooms exist and peak weeks sell out first.
- Ask in writing which drinks are included and the hours they are served.
- In an apartment, Konzum and Studenac supermarkets in Krk Town, Baška, Malinska and Punat cover most needs. Fresh fish is cheaper at morning markets than in restaurants.
- Half-board is the middle option: dinner is covered and lunch can be a €8–12 beach snack or a bakery pizza slice.
- Krk is linked to the mainland by a road bridge, so driving from Rijeka Airport to the hotel takes about 30–45 minutes.

## Bottom Line

For a classic all-inclusive holiday, Krk offers one hotel, and Istria offers more. For flexibility, half-board hotels and apartments are the island's strength.

faq.question: Are there all-inclusive hotels in Krk?
faq.answer: Very few. Hotel Park Punat in Punat is currently listed with an all-inclusive option, and Sunny Baška by Valamar in Baška is promoted for it too. Most other Krk hotels sell breakfast or half-board only.

faq.question: How much does all-inclusive cost in Krk per person?
faq.answer: Roughly €60–100 per person per night in shoulder season and €110–180 in July and August, for adults sharing a room. Child discounts can lower a family's total notably.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive cheaper than half-board in Krk?
faq.answer: No. All-inclusive usually costs about €20–50 more per person per night than half-board. It pays off mainly for families who would otherwise buy lunches, snacks and drinks for several children.

faq.question: Where is the nearest all-inclusive resort to Krk in Croatia?
faq.answer: The nearest is Hotel Park Punat on Krk itself. Beyond the island, Istrian resorts such as Girandella in Rabac, Park Plaza Verudela in Pula and Maistra Select Funtana offer all-inclusive.

faq.question: Is a private apartment cheaper than all-inclusive in Krk?
faq.answer: Yes, by a wide margin. An apartment costs about €25–50 per person per night in peak season, plus €15–25 per day for groceries, against €110–180 for all-inclusive.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive good for families with small children on Krk?
faq.answer: Yes, for short stays. Kids' clubs, buffets and a pool on site reduce planning, and children's rates are low. For stays beyond a week, an apartment near a beach is cheaper and more flexible.
